To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the melanocyte migration is a crucial step in the UVB‐NB induced repigmentation of vitiligo.

1) FAK is expressed by melanocytes in the epidermis and dermis of vitiligo skin, 2) FAK is up‐regulated after NB‐UVB treatment, 3) FAK is involved in melanocyte migration, 4) c‐KIT is expressed in melanocytes in the basal layer of the epidermis in vitiligo skin and 5) c‐KIT expression is increased in melanocytes in NB‐UVB‐responsive lesions,
the repigmentation patterns induced after NB‐UVB treatment in vitiligo are related to the melanocytic migration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship of the repigmentation patterns with the melanocyte migration, differentiation, and proliferation induced by UVB‐NB.
the relationship between melanocyte migration and melanocyte proliferation and the repigmentation pattern in UVB‐NB treated vitiligo.
the repigmentation patterns and the mechanisms involved in the melanocytic migration, proliferation, and differentiation in vitiligo patients treated with UVB‐NB therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

1) FAK expression is higher in the diffuse pattern than in the other repigmentation patterns; 2) c‐KIT is more strongly expressed in the diffuse pattern and in the follicular pattern than in the marginal pattern, which suggests a more active role in the repigmentation process; 3) the unresponsive lesions are characterized by the lack of FAK expression; and 4) the unresponsive vitiligo lesions are characterized by a lack of c‐KIT expression,
the follicular pattern of repigmentation is the most common, followed by the marginal pattern, and finally the diffuse pattern.
the repigmentation patterns induced after NB‐UVB phototherapy are related to the proliferation and differentiation of the melanocytes and the melanocytes' migration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the melanocyte proliferation and differentiation are involved in the repigmentation of the vitiliginous lesions, and that the melanocyte migration is the key factor in the formation of different repigmentation patterns induced with UVB‐NB therapy.

the follicular pattern is the most frequent and it is associated with a high number of melanocytes, whereas the marginal pattern is associated with the lowest number of melanocytes and it is characterized by a high expression of c‐KIT and a low expression of FAK.
the follicular repigmentation was characterized by the highest expression of FAK and the lowest expression of c‐KIT.
The main takeaway from our work is that

melanocyte migration is involved in the formation of follicular and marginal repigmentation patterns, while melanocyte proliferation plays an important role in diffuse and unresponsive repigmentation.
UVB‐NB‐induced repigmentation in vitiligo is featured by three main patterns of repigmentation: follicular, marginal and diffuse.

the follicular pattern is characterized by the presence of a high density of melanocytes and FAK expression in the follicular epithelium, whereas marginal pattern is characterized by a high density of FAK‐positive melanocytes and c‐KIT expression in the follicle epithelium, and diffuse pattern is characterized by FAK and c‐KIT positive melanocytes in the basal layer.
